en.bdb: Among the gurmukhs pervades the Guru

verses.gurmukhi: ਅਮਲੀ ਸੋਫੀ ਚਾਕਰਾਂ ਆਪੁ ਆਪਣੇ ਲਾਗੇ ਬੰਨੇ।
verses.translit_en: amalee sofee chaakaraa(n) aap aapane laage ba(n)ne|

en.bdb: Servants, addict as well as teetotaller, may be in the vicinity, but the minister

verses.gurmukhi: ਮਹਰਮ ਹੋਹਿ ਵਜੀਰ ਸੋ ਮੰਤ੍ਰ ਪਿਆਲਾ ਮੂਲ ਨ ਮੰਨੇ।
verses.translit_en: maharam hoh vajeer so ma(n)tr piaalaa mool na ma(n)ne|

en.bdb: Who knows ins and outs of the court never accepts their advice.

verses.gurmukhi: ਨਾ ਮਹਿਰਮ ਹੁਸਿਆਰ ਮਸਤ ਮਰਦਾਨੀ ਮਜਲਸ ਕਰਿ ਭੰਨੇ।
verses.translit_en: naa mahiram husiaar masat maradhaanee majalas kar bha(n)ne|

en.bdb: The ignorant one who tries to be clever or feigns indifference is expelled by the minister from the court.

verses.gurmukhi: ਤਕਰੀਰੀ ਤਹਰੀਰ ਵਿਚਿ ਪੀਰ ਪਰਸਤ ਮੁਰੀਦ ਉਪੰਨੇ।
verses.translit_en: takareeree tahareer vich peer parasat mureedh upa(n)ne|

en.bdb: In speaking and writing like this minister, loyal devoted disciples, have been created by the Guru.

verses.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਮਤਿ ਅਲਖੁ ਨ ਲਖੀਐ ਅਮਲੀ ਸੂਫੀ ਲਗੈ ਨ ਕੰਨੇ।
verses.translit_en: gurmat alakh na lakheeaai amalee soofee lagai na ka(n)ne|

en.bdb: Those addicts, who have not had the glimpse of the Lord through the wisdom of the Guru, never associate with the teetotallers (the holy ones).

verses.gurmukhi: ਅਮਲੀ ਜਾਣਨਿ ਅਮਲੀਆਂ ਸੋਫੀ ਜਾਣਨਿ ਸੋਫੀ ਵੰਨੇ।
verses.translit_en: amalee jaanan amaleeaa(n) sofee jaanan sofee va(n)ne|

en.bdb: The addicts are acquainted with addicts, likewise, teetotallers meet the teetotallers.

verses.gurmukhi: ਹੇਤੁ ਵਜੀਰੈ ਪਾਤਿਸਾਹ ਦੁਇ ਖੋੜੀ ਇਕੁ ਜੀਉ ਸਿਧੰਨੇ।
verses.translit_en: het vajeerai paatisaeh dhui khoRee ik jeeau sidha(n)ne|

en.bdb: The affection between a king and his minister is such as if the same one life current is moving in two bodies.

verses.gurmukhi: ਜਿਉ ਸਮਸੇਰ ਮਿਆਨ ਵਿਚਿ ਇਕਤੁ ਥੋਕੁ ਰਹਨ ਦੁਇ ਖੰਨੇ।
verses.translit_en: jiau samaser miaan vich ikat thok rahan dhui kha(n)ne|

en.bdb: This relationship is also like the relation of the sword in the sheath; the two may be separate, yet they are one ( i.e. sword in sheath is yet called sword only).
Likewise is the relation of gurmukhs with the Guru; they are subsumed in each other in such a manner as is the juice and the sugarcane.
